text:
Wednesday, November 28, 2018
Get the Morning Brief sent directly to your inbox every Monday to Friday by 6:30 a.m. ET. Subscribe
What to watch today Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell will be speaking at the Economic Club of New York at 12 p.m. ET on Wednesday. Powell is expected to deliver prepared remarks before answering pre-drafted questions from members of the Economic Club. The Fed’s language has been very closely watched lately as volatility continues to seep back into the market. Though it had been widely expected that the Fed would raise interest rates in December, the Fed’s recent shift to a slightly more dovish tone has been keeping market watchers on edge.

Top news (Photo credit: JIM WATSON/AFP/Getty Images) More Trump has the GM problem backward : President Donald Trump tweet-threatened to cut federal subsidies for electric cars General Motors ( GM ) sells, and said he was “very disappointed” in GM and its CEO, Mary Barra. But Trump can’t single out one company to be excluded from subsidies Congress established by law. Trump wants GM to continue building money-losing cars nobody wants to buy in order to save several thousand industrial-era jobs. It’s the exact opposite of what Trump should be encouraging American companies to do, and it’s the wrong message for workers, too. [Yahoo Finance]
More on Trump:
Trump says he’s ‘not even a little bit happy’ with Fed Chair Powell Microsoft becomes world’s most valuable company after Apple rout : Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares rose 0.6% Tuesday, pushing the company’s market value to $828.1 billion at the close. That exceeded by more than $1 billion the value of Apple ( AAPL ), which has tumbled this month on concern about iPhone unit sales. The last time Microsoft’s market capitalization was bigger than Apple was in 2010, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. [Bloomberg]
Papa John’s loses a potential bidder : Trian Fund Management LP, which was evaluating a bid, has decided not to pursue it, according to people familiar with the matter. Papa John’s ( PZZA ) is in the midst of a sale process that began in August. While some bidders remain interested in potentially taking a stake, none is currently considering buying the whole company, these people said. [The Wall Street Journal]
Salesforce beats estimates, shares rise : Salesforce.com Inc. ( CRM ) easily beat analysts’ estimates for quarterly earnings and forecast 2020 revenue above expectations on Tuesday, as more companies turn to its cloud-based services. The company’s shares rose 8% in extended trading, set to add to their about 25% gain this year. [Reuters]
YouTube shifts to make new exclusive shows, movies free : YouTube plans to make all future original programing available to users for free with advertising, as the video streaming unit of Alphabet Inc’s Google ( GOOGL ) seeks a bigger audience for shows and movies that had mostly been restricted to paid subscribers. [Reuters]
